Task S002 / v0.9.33

Christian Verrecchia · 22 November 2026 · internally tested development preview; independent physical/commercial qualification pending.

1. Objective, physical model, equations, units, boundaries, algorithm and limits

# Linear open / simultaneous short measurements — S002

Solve a linear 2D or 3D model with **Matrix** enabled. In **Inductance**, select the driven electrical winding and tick every winding to short. Unticked windings stay open (zero current). Calculate and save the measurement JSON, which includes the exact supplied electrical matrix, its SHA256, selected stable IDs, all cancellation currents and linkages, the accepted source project and solver metadata. `three_winding_2d` is a reproducible example. Equal display names do not connect sources; original canonical series membership defines the electrical matrix.

This is lossless linear matrix postprocessing. It does not start a field job or overwrite the accepted field/project. Re-solve with the exported currents for a field plot of the shorted condition. Nonlinear/AC results without a real static matrix have no control. Singular/nearly dependent ideal ports are rejected; there is no guessed pseudoinverse or resistance regularization.

For a reciprocal positive definite matrix in henries, lambda = L i (Wb turn), W = i^T L i / 2 (J). Let p be the driven port, S the shorted set and all other currents zero. Setting i_p = 1 A and lambda_S = 0 gives i_S = -L_SS^{-1} L_Sp A and L_input = L_pp - L_pS L_SS^{-1} L_Sp. This accounts for mutual coupling between all shorted windings, unlike separate pairwise short measurements. Shorted currents can have either sign. For nonzero-frequency sinusoidal excitation, these conditions correspond to ideal zero-resistance shorts and zero incremental/trapped flux; they are not a resistive AC or transient solution.

The implementation scales by sqrt(L_ii), checks normalized reciprocity (<=1e-6), explicitly symmetrizes that qualified numerical discrepancy, and uses Cholesky factors plus triangular substitutions. Every normalized energy pivot must exceed 1e-10. This is an independence guard, not a condition-number or physical-error bound. Full-matrix positivity is required. Energy and shorted-linkage residuals must be <=1e-8 in the documented normalization. The exact original unsymmetrized input matrix and discrepancy remain in the export.

Open-input L_pp is self inductance. The difference between open and shorted input inductance is cancelled coupling; neither value defines a unique magnetising/leakage T-network decomposition. No turns-ratio assumption, core-only flux partition or arbitrary Lm label is introduced. These values are not interchangeable with the OpenMagnetics adviser's model-specific Lm/leakage definitions without a matched model and equivalent-circuit convention.

Actual reference tests re-solve the prescribed cancellation currents on independent 2D H1 and 3D edge-element fields. The 338-triangle planar model gives open1216.731151958µH / both-short119.418354605µH. The 2940-tetrahedron spatial ideal-sheet model gives open168.095713276µH / both-short131.482603490µH. Their field-energy prediction differences are8.71e-12 /4.55e-11 relative. These are same-model algebra/field consistency checks on coarse meshes, not mesh/domain convergence, finite-copper validation or Maxwell/hardware evidence. Original material/source/boundary equations are unchanged: closed Az=0 planar boundary with depth scaling; tangential-A=0 spatial boundary and ideal closed sheet sources.

Reproduce using `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_port_reduction.py -v` and `python verification/run_s002_cases.py` from the source root. Optional SciPy accelerates original reference solves; the new reduction itself uses only the Python standard library. Reports/evidence generators, Node/DOM/Wasm/browser QA packages are development tools, not additional desktop runtime dependencies.

Remaining work includes independent source/mesh/p/domain accuracy, joined finite winding/return/core coupling, consistent generated-candidate FEM comparison, native nonlinear/AC, full CLLC and independent commercial/hardware validation. Clean permitted Windows10/11 offline checks without Python installed remain pending; development CI smoke is narrower.

The original matrix is obtained by unit source solves: L_ij = b_i^T K^-1 b_j. Canonical same-current section grouping sums their linkage and source basis. The matrix reduction uses those electrical ports; a named circuit container is not a connection. The API postprocesses the supplied matrix and validates algebraic consistency; it does not authenticate arbitrary caller data as a solved FEM result. The original UI passes the accepted field matrix and exports its accepted project.

For 2D, -div(nu grad Az)=Jz with Az=0 at the outer boundary, B=curl(Az ez), prescribed paired Jz=±NI/area and original stack depth. For 3D, curl(nu curl A)=J with closed ideal sheet sources, the original edge-element gauge and tangential A=0 exterior. nu [m/H], A [Wb/m], B [T], J [A/m²], lambda [Wb turn], L [H], W [J]. No finite copper, resistive short, nonlinear tangent, loaded resonant network or new boundary/source discretization is introduced.

Separate pairwise shorts do not enforce the simultaneous mutual constraints. The analytical matrix in tests has exact simultaneous L=48/7 µH, i_s=-4/7 and i_t=-5/7 A per input ampere. Port reversal and short-order permutations preserve input inductance. Rejection checks include nonpositive, exact/near singular, nonreciprocal, malformed, nonfinite and ambiguous selections.

0007  def reduce_ports(circuits, input_id, shorted_ids):  #: Eliminate only the explicitly shorted electrical ports; all other currents remain zero.
0008      if not isinstance(circuits,dict):raise ValueError('A solved linear electrical-winding matrix is required')  #: Reject missing/nonlinear/AC result formats before any arithmetic.

0011      n=len(ids)  #: Keep all matrix indexing tied to the explicit stable port order.
0012      if not isinstance(names,list) or len(names)!=n or any(not isinstance(k,str) for k in names):raise ValueError('Every electrical port needs a display name')  #: Equal labels remain allowed because they do not define connectivity.
0013      if not isinstance(raw,list) or len(raw)!=n or any(not isinstance(row,list) or len(row)!=n for row in raw):raise ValueError('Require a square electrical inductance matrix')  #: Reject ragged, missing and mismatched source data.
0014      if any(type(v) not in (int,float) or not math.isfinite(v) for row in raw for v in row):raise ValueError('Inductance entries must be finite real henries')  #: Refuse booleans, strings and complex/undefined AC equivalents.
0015      if input_id not in ids or not isinstance(shorted_ids,list) or any(not isinstance(k,str) or k not in ids for k in shorted_ids) or len(set(shorted_ids))!=len(shorted_ids) or input_id in shorted_ids:raise ValueError('Select one input and distinct other shorted port IDs')  #: Prevent duplicate constraints, accidental input shorting and unknown winding selections.
0016      if any(raw[i][i]<=0 for i in range(n)):raise ValueError('All port self inductances must be positive')  #: A zero-energy or invalid source cannot define an independent characterized port.
0017      scales=[math.sqrt(raw[i][i]) for i in range(n)]  #: Normalize turn-count and unit-scale disparities before testing numerical independence.
0018      reciprocity=max(abs(raw[i][j]/scales[i]/scales[j]-raw[j][i]/scales[i]/scales[j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(n))  #: Measure reciprocity in dimensionless port coordinates.

0020      normalized=[[(raw[i][j]/scales[i]/scales[j]+raw[j][i]/scales[i]/scales[j])/2 for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]  #: Explicitly average only reciprocity-qualified roundoff/asymmetric solver error.

0022          lower=[[0.]*len(indices) for _ in indices];pivots=[]  #: Retain dimensionless Cholesky factors and independence diagnostics.
0023          for a,i in enumerate(indices):  #: Factor the selected principal block in its exact declared order.
0024              for b,j in enumerate(indices[:a+1]):  #: Compute only the reciprocal lower triangle.
0025                  value=normalized[i][j]-math.fsum(lower[a][k]*lower[b][k] for k in range(b))  #: Subtract previously resolved quadratic-energy components.
0026                  if a==b:  #: A diagonal pivot tests a new independent source direction.
0027                      if value<=1e-10:raise ValueError('Matrix is nonpositive or nearly dependent; ideal/redundant ports require a qualified constraint model')  #: Reject singular and ill-conditioned modes instead of inventing a pseudoinverse.
0028                      pivots.append(value);lower[a][b]=math.sqrt(value)  #: Retain the actual normalized pivot, not an accuracy certificate.
0029                  else:lower[a][b]=value/lower[b][b]  #: Complete this off-diagonal factor coefficient.
0030          return lower,pivots  #: Preserve factors for substitution and diagnostics for the exported record.
0031      _,pivots=factor(list(range(n)))  #: Require the entire supplied electrical matrix to describe independent positive-energy ports.
0032      p=ids.index(input_id);shorts=[ids.index(k) for k in shorted_ids];lower,_=factor(shorts);forward=[]  #: Preserve user-selected short order while retaining exact global IDs.
0033      for a,s in enumerate(shorts):forward.append((-normalized[s][p]-math.fsum(lower[a][b]*forward[b] for b in range(a)))/lower[a][a])  #: Solve the lower-triangular system for normalized cancellation currents.
0034      solution=[0.]*len(shorts)  #: Allocate only the selected shorted-current unknowns.
0035      for a in range(len(shorts)-1,-1,-1):solution[a]=(forward[a]-math.fsum(lower[b][a]*solution[b] for b in range(a+1,len(shorts))))/lower[a][a]  #: Back-substitute to solve C_SS x = -C_Sp.
0036      currents=[0.]*n;currents[p]=1.  #: Normalize to exactly one input ampere and leave every other open port current zero.
0037      for s,value in zip(shorts,solution):currents[s]=value*scales[p]/scales[s]  #: Transform the normalized solution back to amperes per input ampere.
0038      matrix=[[normalized[i][j]*scales[i]*scales[j] for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]  #: Recover the disclosed reciprocal matrix in physical henries.

0045      digest=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(source,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':'),allow_nan=False).encode()).hexdigest()  #: Bind the report to original IDs/order/labels and exact input matrix values.

0001  """Reference-only JSON bridge for the original interface inside a Pyodide worker."""
0002  import importlib  #: Resolve only explicitly whitelisted original metadata/model adapters.
0003  import json  #: Keep browser requests and numerical results finite and portable.
0004  from pathlib import Path  #: Read the same bundled examples and original builder data.
0005  from .project import validate  #: Preserve all original material/source/electrical membership guards.
0006  from .connections import require_static_sources  #: Reject AC solids on every static field action.
0007  from .analysis import solve_project,convergence,current_sweep,mesh_public  #: Reuse exact original field, study and export data.
0008  from .adaptive import adaptive_solve  #: Reuse actual original reference refinement.
0009  from .ac import solve_ac,frequency_sweep  #: Preserve dedicated reference complex-field solving.
0010  from .mesh import build_mesh  #: Preserve original mesh generation.
0011  from .export import field_csv,vtk,report_html  #: Reuse exact field export schemas and physical units.
0012  ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]  #: Resolve the actual virtual source tree, not remote files.
0013  ACTIONS={'mesh','solve','convergence','sweep','adaptive','ac','ac_sweep'}  #: Keep unavailable native code visibly outside browser capabilities.
0014  ROUTES={'/api/builder/catalog':('builder','catalog',[]),'/api/builder/upgrade':('workflow','upgrade',['specification']),'/api/builder/build':('builder','build',['specification']),'/api/builder/mas-export':('mas_exchange','export_exchange',['specification','options']),'/api/builder/mas-restore':('mas_exchange','restore_exchange',['packet','mode']),'/api/builder/mas-core-export':('mas_core_geometry','export_core_geometry',['specification']),'/api/builder/mas-core-apply':('mas_core_geometry','apply_core_geometry',['packet','mode']),'/api/builder/mas-material-export':('mas_material','export_material',['specification']),'/api/builder/mas-material-apply':('mas_material','apply_material',['packet','mode']),'/api/bobbin-draft':('bobbin_cad','draft_bobbin',['project']),'/api/turn-ports-draft':('turn_ports','draft_ports',['project']),'/api/turn-links-draft':('turn_links','draft_links',['project','turn_ports']),'/api/turn-links-plan':('turn_links','link_plan',['project','turn_ports','turn_links'])}  #: Share original builder/MAS/source-draft functionality through an explicit callable whitelist.
0015  
0016  
0017  def preflight(request):  #: Validate before the browser replaces its previous accepted job or result.
0018      action=request.get('action','solve')  #: Preserve the original default reference solve.
0019      if action not in ACTIONS:raise ValueError('This native action requires the Windows desktop build; online preview runs reference solvers')  #: Never fabricate native adviser/CAD/FEM availability.
0020      project=validate(request['project'])  #: Validate a detached complete original FEM model.
0021      if action in {'solve','convergence','sweep','adaptive'}:require_static_sources(project)  #: Preserve static/AC source separation and independent winding identity.
0022      d=project['domain'];cells=d['nx']*d['ny']*(d.get('nz',1)*6 if project['mode']=='3d' else 2)  #: Bound initial reference work using actual grid dimensions.
0023      if cells>24000:raise ValueError('Online preview initial mesh budget is 24000 cells; use the desktop build for larger studies')  #: Make the additional browser resource ceiling explicit rather than truncate geometry.
0024      return project  #: Retain original project semantics without editing the source design.
0025  
0026  
0027  def run(request,progress=None):  #: Perform genuine numerical work inside the cancellable browser worker.
0028      project=preflight(request);action=request.get('action','solve');matrix=bool(request.get('matrix',True))  #: Reuse authoritative physical preflight at execution time too.
0029      if action=='mesh':return {'project':project,'mesh':mesh_public(build_mesh(project,progress)),'kind':'mesh'}  #: Return an actual original mesh, never a display-only placeholder.

0038  def rpc(path,data=None):  #: Share original metadata/validation/import adapters without a Python HTTP server.
0039      data=data or {}  #: Keep read-only metadata calls independent of a request body.
0040      if path=='/api/session':return dict(token='browser-local',version='0.9.33',examples=[p.stem for p in sorted((ROOT/'examples').glob('*.json')) if p.name!='transformer_design_request.json'])  #: Preserve original menu contents and explicit browser build identity.
0041      if path=='/api/backends':return dict(design_transformer=False,ngsolve=False,openmagnetics=False,geometry_cad=False,packages={},geometry_cad_packages={},runtime='Pyodide reference preview')  #: Make unavailable compiled native dependencies explicit to existing controls.
0042      if path.startswith('/api/example/') or path=='/api/designer/example':  #: Return the exact original source examples through the virtual filesystem.
0043          name=path.rsplit('/',1)[-1] if path!='/api/designer/example' else 'transformer_design_request';allowed={p.stem:p for p in (ROOT/'examples').glob('*.json')}  #: Bind reads to known example names, preventing traversal.
0044          if name not in allowed:raise ValueError('Unknown example')  #: Reject arbitrary virtual filesystem reads.

0057          module,name,args=ROUTES[path];value=getattr(importlib.import_module('.'+module,__package__),name)(*[data.get(a) for a in args])  #: Call only a declared function with declared JSON argument keys.

0104                      if 'fields' in result:

0117                      self.job['error'] = str(e)

0119          return job_id

0013  <dialog id="guideDialog"><div class="dialog-head"><h2>Engineering workflow</h2><button data-close="guideDialog">×</button></div><div class="guide"><p class="eyebrow">MAGNETICS STUDIO 0.8 · INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION</p><h3>Guided builder</h3><p>Click Builder and follow Core type → Dimensions → Material → Air gaps → Circuits → Windings → Interleaving → Nameplate/build. The same circuit and winding inputs drive 2D and 3D geometry.</p><h3>Circuits and independent windings</h3><p>A named circuit, such as Phase U, contains its own winding count and winding definitions. Primary and secondary have independent turns, current and phase. Only physical layers of one electrical winding carry the same series current. Reorder those layers per limb to define interleaving. Single, multilayer and interleaved arrangements are supported. Declared totals and odd final layers are checked.</p><p>Signed instantaneous current is the default excitation. Optional sinusoidal snapshot mode uses peak current × cos(snapshot angle + winding phase). It is a prescribed magnetostatic point, not a voltage-driven or AC circuit solve. Phase names do not impose phase angles.</p><h3>Material and image digitiser</h3><p>Select a material, enter linear μr, import numeric B–H data, or click Digitise from graph image in Material. Load a screenshot, enter graph limits/units/scales and calibrate A=(Xmin,Ymin), B=(Xmax,Ymin), C=(Xmin,Ymax). Trace one monotonic positive branch. Scroll zooms; Shift/right-drag pans. Move/delete points or edit their SI values. Invalid points block application; including (0,0) is an explicit assumption. Images stay in the local browser. Perspective photographs are not corrected.</p><p>Nonlinear reversible B–H is available in 2D. 3D remains linear; storing a curve in 3D does not activate nonlinear physics. Temperature/frequency labels select curve data explicitly; no automatic scaling or loss model is implied.</p><h3>2D and 3D windings</h3><p>2D supports full winding-block rectangles or separately meshed round/litz/foil/rectangular turn sections. A region carrying n turns has Jz = ±nI/A. Each winding has both + and − sections, preserving total ampere-turns. Round curves are faceted polygons. Litz is homogenized within each bundle, not resolved strand by strand. Stack depth scales linkage and energy; planar end effects are absent.</p><p>3D uses closed ideal rectangular current sheets at the packing-defined mean radius and axial extent. It computes 3D field end effects in a finite air domain. Winding display envelopes do not represent finite-copper eddy-current physics. Curved toroidal 3D cores and individual 3D wires are not implemented.</p><h3>Mesh, solve and inspect</h3><p>Preview and check fit, then use the model in the workspace, generate mesh and solve. Standard 3D budget is 44k tetrahedra; the explicitly selected extended budget allows 120k and may be slower. The builder shows a mesh estimate. Uncheck Matrix for field-only analysis. Failed convergence is rejected.</p><p>Use 3D field volume for magnitude colours, volume arrows, traced B paths, transparency and capped core surfaces. Rotating field slice remains a single plane. Streamlines are approximate postprocessing of elementwise fields. The solid model view provides part selection, hiding, cutaway and display OBJ export.</p><h3>Results and verification</h3><p>Linear inductance uses independent unit excitations. Native 3D section matrices are grouped by electrical winding, not by circuit container. Per-container winding-pair leakage assumes the selected other winding is shorted and all remaining winding currents are zero/open; the full coupled matrix is retained. Nonlinear points do not have a constant linear inductance matrix.</p><p>Check finer mesh and larger air boundaries. A tiny algebraic residual or energy discrepancy alone is not evidence of engineering accuracy. The closed outer boundary imposes zero normal flux and is not an infinite open boundary. Sharp-corner field peaks can remain mesh dependent.</p><h3>Save and reuse</h3><p>Save project JSON for the workspace, builder input JSON for the recipe, or a digitiser session including the source graph image. Changing raw generated geometry flags the recipe as stale; rebuilding does not infer manual edits. Previous v0.5 recipes migrate with their explicit geometry preserved. CSV, JSON, VTK, PNG and self-contained HTML reports remain available.</p><h3>Release boundaries</h3><p>Independent research software with limited validation. Linear 2D AC/eddy-current analysis is available with explicit solid-conductor current constraints and RMS phasors. No 3D/nonlinear AC, transient, core-loss, hysteresis, thermal, permanent-magnet, force/torque, arbitrary CAD or general 3D adaptive-meshing solver is added. Linear 2D local residual-driven refinement is available from Analysis; its indicator is not a certified error bound. The circuit hierarchy is a modelling definition, not a general electrical network solver.</p></div></dialog>

0010  def build(destination):  #: Generate a complete, source-bound browser preview without a Python server.
0011      destination=Path(destination);destination.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);files={}  #: Preserve an explicit static output and trusted virtual source packet.
0012      for folder in ['engine','examples','data']:  #: Include exact original reference kernels, physical examples and builder/material inputs.

0022      (destination/'magnetics-core.json').write_text(json.dumps({'files':files},ensure_ascii=False),encoding='utf-8')  #: Ship trusted original Python and inputs without any saved field pretending to be a new solve.

0001  """Build a Windows one-folder development preview with installed native dependencies."""
0002  import argparse  #: Keep the exact output and build platform explicit.
0003  import importlib.metadata as metadata  #: Inventory actual distributions and preserve upstream licence files.
0004  import json  #: Record exact packaged source and dependency provenance.
0005  from pathlib import Path  #: Resolve trusted application resources and native wheel members.
0006  import shutil  #: Copy exact runtime notices and deterministic source snapshots.
0007  import subprocess  #: Invoke PyInstaller through the selected build interpreter.
0008  import sys  #: Require a real Windows host and preserve its actual Python interpreter.
0009  ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]  #: Bind the build to this exact delivered checkout.
0010  
0011  
0012  def main():  #: Produce a complete one-folder Windows preview rather than cross-label a Linux executable.
0013      parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);parser.add_argument('output',type=Path);args=parser.parse_args()  #: Require an explicit distribution parent directory.
0014      if sys.platform!='win32':raise ValueError('Build this Windows package on a permitted Windows host')  #: Do not produce a platform-mislabeled application executable.

+"""Explicit simultaneous shorts: analytical algebra, actual 2D/3D fields and HTTP state."""
+import copy  #: Preserve original winding identities while constructing independent physical secondary sources.
+import json  #: Retain reproducible exact matrices, solved fields and characterization evidence.
+import math  #: Independently evaluate energy and current/flux normalization checks.
+from pathlib import Path  #: Resolve actual shipped physical models.
+import threading  #: Run the genuine protected HTTP server for state-retention checks.
+import unittest  #: Record distinct physical and rejection contracts.
+from urllib.request import Request,urlopen  #: Exercise real loopback routes rather than a mocked request handler.
+from engine.analysis import solve_project  #: Re-solve independently prescribed cancellation currents on the actual field mesh.
+from engine.browser_bridge import rpc  #: Verify genuine online/desktop shared postprocessing.
+from engine.port_reduction import reduce_ports  #: Exercise the actual declared electrical-port reduction.
+from studio import make_server  #: Check API integration without changing accepted jobs/results.
+ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]  #: Keep fixture lookup rooted in the delivered checkout.
+
+
+def three_ports(mode):  #: Build distinct secondary geometry while keeping equal display names electrically independent.
+    p=json.loads((ROOT/'examples'/('transformer_2d.json' if mode=='2d' else 'air_coil_3d.json')).read_text());p['domain'].update(nx=5,ny=5)  #: Use genuine fitted field models and bounded but nontrivial meshes.
+    if mode=='2d':  #: Split the original secondary window into two separately driven physical conductors.
+        p['windings'].append(dict(id='tertiary',name='Secondary',turns=13,current=0))  #: Preserve equal labels with distinct stable electrical IDs.
+        for region in list(p['regions']):  #: Give both new secondary source halves their own fitted geometry.
+            if region.get('winding')=='secondary':  #: Keep the original positive and return source directions.
+                region['y1']=.062;third=copy.deepcopy(region);third.update(id=region['id']+'_third',winding='tertiary',y0=.065,y1=.072);p['regions'].append(third)  #: Create spatially distinct paired conductors instead of identical redundant source modes.
+    else:  #: Use three actual closed rectangular sheet sources with different axial support.
+        p['domain']['nz']=5;first=p['windings'][0];first.update(current=1,series_group='primary')  #: Retain the original main 3D winding and an explicit grouped electrical key.
+        for i,(z0,z1) in enumerate([(.025,.042),(.078,.095)]):  #: Position the two secondary sheets at different heights.
+            w=copy.deepcopy(first);w.update(id='secondary'+str(i),name='Secondary',series_group='secondary'+str(i),turns=17+i,current=0);w['window'].update(z0=z0,z1=z1);p['windings'].append(w)  #: Preserve physical source identity, polarity and independent current assignment.
+    return p  #: Return a detached complete physical source project.
+
+
+class PortReductionTests(unittest.TestCase):  #: Verify circuit semantics through actual magnetic energy/linkage, not only formula repetition.
+    def test_analytical_three_port_simultaneous_and_orientation(self):  #: Compare against a hand-solvable coupled 3×3 matrix and signed source reversal.
+        c=dict(group_ids=['p','s','t'],names=['P','same','same'],inductance_H=[[v*1e-6 for v in row] for row in [[10,3,2],[3,4,1],[2,1,2]]]);original=copy.deepcopy(c)  #: Preserve an explicit positive-energy analytical fixture with two equal labels.
+        r=reduce_ports(c,'p',['s','t']);self.assertAlmostEqual(r['input_inductance_H']/1e-6,48/7);self.assertAlmostEqual(r['current_A_per_input_A'][1],-4/7);self.assertAlmostEqual(r['current_A_per_input_A'][2],-5/7)  #: Check simultaneous coupling against exact rational cancellation currents and Lsc.
+        self.assertLess(r['input_inductance_H'],reduce_ports(c,'p',['s'])['input_inductance_H']);self.assertLess(r['input_inductance_H'],reduce_ports(c,'p',['t'])['input_inductance_H'])  #: Demonstrate why separate pairwise measurements cannot replace simultaneous shorts.
+        c['inductance_H']=[[x*(-1 if (i==1)!=(j==1) else 1) for j,x in enumerate(row)] for i,row in enumerate(c['inductance_H'])];reversed_port=reduce_ports(c,'p',['t','s'])  #: Reverse one physical port orientation and reorder the declared short list.
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(reversed_port['input_inductance_H']/r['input_inductance_H'],1);self.assertAlmostEqual(reversed_port['current_A_per_input_A'][1],4/7);self.assertEqual(original, r['source_matrix'])  #: Preserve invariant input inductance, signed current reversal and exact original-matrix export.
+
+    def test_reject_bad_and_dependent_modes_without_mutation(self):  #: Fail closed for invalid, nonpassive and nearly dependent electrical matrices.
+        c=dict(group_ids=['a','b'],names=['same','same'],inductance_H=[[1.,.3],[.3,.5]])  #: Use independent positive-energy ports with equal display names.
+        for matrix in [[[1,2],[2,1]],[[1,1],[1,1]],[[1,1-1e-12],[1-1e-12,1]],[[1,.2],[.3,1]],[[1,True],[True,1]],[[1,float('nan')],[0,1]],[[0,0],[0,1]]]:  #: Exercise indefiniteness, exact/near singularity, nonreciprocity, types, finiteness and zero source energy.
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):reduce_ports({**c,'inductance_H':matrix},'a',['b'])  #: Never produce fabricated cancellation currents from an unqualified matrix.
+        for selected in [['a'],['b','b'],['missing'],'b']:  #: Include input shorting, duplicate and malformed selections.
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):reduce_ports(c,'a',selected)  #: Retain explicit ID-based constraints.
+        saved=copy.deepcopy(c);r=reduce_ports(c,'a',[]);self.assertEqual(r['input_inductance_H'],1);self.assertEqual(c,saved);self.assertEqual(r['open_ids'],['b'])  #: An empty short set means open input; postprocessing never edits source JSON.
+        scaled={**c,'inductance_H':[[1e-12,3e-7],[3e-7,.5]]};self.assertAlmostEqual(reduce_ports(scaled,'a',['b'])['input_inductance_H']/1e-12,.82)  #: Diagonal normalization handles extreme legitimate turn/unit scales without an absolute-henry pivot threshold.
+
+    def test_actual_planar_and_spatial_cancellation_energy(self):  #: Compare predicted currents with independently re-solved actual vector fields and source work in both dimensions.
+        for mode in ['2d','3d']:  #: Exercise distinct planar H1 and spatial edge-element formulations.
+            p=three_ports(mode);source=copy.deepcopy(p);solved=solve_project(p);c=solved['circuits'];report=reduce_ports(c,c['group_ids'][0],c['group_ids'][1:])  #: Compute a full genuine unit-excitation matrix before any reduction.
+            q=copy.deepcopy(solved['project'])  #: Prescribe the independently calculated cancellation currents on the exact accepted physical project.
+            from engine.connections import series_key  #: Map currents back through the authoritative canonical electrical grouping.
+            for w in q['windings']:w['current']=report['current_A_per_input_A'][c['group_ids'].index(series_key(w))]  #: Assign every physical section of an electrical winding the same calculated current.
+            check=solve_project(q,False);links=[sum(w['linkage_Wb_turn'] for w,physical in zip(check['windings'],q['windings']) if series_key(physical)==key) for key in c['group_ids']]  #: Recompute actual field linkages with no matrix solve and regroup independently.
+            scale=report['input_open_H'];self.assertLess(max(abs(x) for x in links[1:])/scale,2e-7);self.assertAlmostEqual(links[0]/report['input_inductance_H'],1,places=6)  #: Require actual zero short linkage and the predicted driven-input flux/current.
+            self.assertAlmostEqual(2*check['stats']['energy_J']/report['input_inductance_H'],1,places=6);self.assertGreater(check['stats']['peak_B_T'],0);self.assertEqual(p,source)  #: Check independent physical field energy, nonzero B and source immutability.
+            self.assertEqual(rpc('/api/port-reduction',dict(circuits=c,input_id=c['group_ids'][0],shorted_ids=c['group_ids'][1:])),report)  #: Keep the real browser bridge identical to direct characterization.
+
+    def test_real_protected_http_preserves_accepted_state(self):  #: Characterization must not replace or mutate a prior accepted field/job.
+        server=make_server();state=server.studio_state;thread=threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever,daemon=True);thread.start()  #: Exercise an actual protected loopback server on an allocated port.
+        try:  #: Always release real HTTP resources after success or rejection.
+            state.job=dict(id='accepted',status='done');state.field_result={'sentinel':'unchanged'};state.result_job='accepted'  #: Establish explicit accepted workspace state independently of characterization.
+            data=dict(circuits=dict(group_ids=['a','b'],names=['same','same'],inductance_H=[[1.,.3],[.3,.5]]),input_id='a',shorted_ids=['b'])  #: Submit an explicit supplied matrix; the API does not claim to authenticate arbitrary matrices as FEM evidence.
+            request=Request('http://127.0.0.1:'+str(server.server_port)+'/api/port-reduction',data=json.dumps(data).encode(),headers={'X-Studio-Token':state.token,'Content-Type':'application/json'})  #: Retain genuine session/body/host guards.
+            with urlopen(request) as response:r=json.load(response)  #: Read actual finite JSON returned by the server.
+            self.assertAlmostEqual(r['input_inductance_H'],.82);self.assertEqual(state.result_job,'accepted');self.assertEqual(state.field_result,{'sentinel':'unchanged'});self.assertEqual(state.job['status'],'done')  #: Check physical reduction and unchanged accepted job/result.
+        finally:server.shutdown();server.server_close();thread.join()  #: Close the genuine server and supervision thread.
+
+
+if __name__=='__main__':unittest.main()  #: Support a reproducible focused source-form numerical run.

0066          with:

+"""S002 actual field/current/energy evidence generator; development QA only."""
+import copy  #: Keep original physical projects and prescribed-current verification cases detached.
+import json  #: Save complete actual solved fields and explicit reduction reports reproducibly.
+from pathlib import Path  #: Resolve source, tests and retained actual numerical evidence.
+import sys  #: Import the exact delivered field and physical-model test helpers.
+ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1];sys.path[:0]=[str(ROOT),str(ROOT/'tests')]  #: Bind this generator to delivered source rather than an installed copy.
+from test_port_reduction import three_ports  #: Reuse declared actual planar and spatial three-port fixtures.
+from engine.analysis import solve_project  #: Execute genuine matrix and independent prescribed-current field solves.
+from engine.connections import series_key  #: Assign every physical series section to its stable electrical port.
+from engine.port_reduction import reduce_ports  #: Execute the shipped simultaneous-short implementation.
+DATA=ROOT/'sample_results/port_reduction';DATA.mkdir(exist_ok=True);summary={}  #: Retain new evidence separately from all historical solved JSON.
+for mode in ['2d','3d']:  #: Record applicability separately for both original magnetic formulations.
+    result=solve_project(three_ports(mode));c=result['circuits'];report=reduce_ports(c,c['group_ids'][0],c['group_ids'][1:]);project=copy.deepcopy(result['project'])  #: Extract a genuine multiport matrix and explicitly select both secondaries.
+    for winding in project['windings']:winding['current']=report['current_A_per_input_A'][c['group_ids'].index(series_key(winding))]  #: Prescribe calculated cancellation currents on every original source section.
+    check=solve_project(project,False);packet=dict(matrix_solve=result,measurement=report,prescribed_current_solve=check)  #: Retain both complete actual field solves and the exact supplied-matrix reduction.
+    (DATA/(mode+'.json')).write_text(json.dumps(packet,indent=2,allow_nan=False)+'\n')  #: Preserve reproducible field arrays, projects, meshes and solver diagnostics in finite SI JSON.
+    summary[mode]=dict(elements=result['stats']['elements'],input_open_H=report['input_open_H'],input_short_H=report['input_inductance_H'],currents_A=report['current_A_per_input_A'],actual_linkages_Wb_turn=[w['linkage_Wb_turn'] for w in check['windings']],actual_energy_J=check['stats']['energy_J'],relative_energy_prediction=abs(2*check['stats']['energy_J']/report['input_inductance_H']-1),relative_reciprocity=report['normalized_reciprocity_error'])  #: Record actual physical outputs and direct field-versus-reduction consistency, not an external accuracy estimate.
+(DATA/'numerical_summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2)+'\n');print(json.dumps(summary,indent=2))  #: Keep concise and complete actual SI evidence tied to the saved full cases.
